correctness.rationale: For every n>=1 over C, two explicit free-Gm quotient charts cover X_n. The x-nonzero chart quotient is A^(n+2); the x-zero boundary in the u1-nonzero chart is A1*(Gm)^n, cut out by globally regular q=xu1, hence the normal line is trivial. The complement is contractible and tubular-neighborhood homotopy pushout identifies the quotient with the line Thom space, a double suspension of a based n-torus. Iterated product-suspension splitting gives the full wedge-of-spheres equivalence and integral ring, not merely Betti numbers. Independent finite monomial checks returned VERIFY_OK; the infinite proof is geometric/topological.
